name: dsh-kit
description: Deployment kit for DeepSeek Harness plus the model-gate plugin. This manifest is what makes the kit's own context_* tools answer for the kit, and what the ratchet section below compiles into laws the kit checks itself against.

rules.statement: Every agent, subagent and worker runs on a Flash-class DeepSeek model; no non-Flash tier is selected or delegated to.
rules.pendingReason: the model-gate plugin vetoes a non-Flash model at the llm/stream waterfall, and scripts/verify-upgrade.sh probes exactly that ("disallowed model vetoed, Flash model admitted"); what is still unbuilt is a check that the veto is INSTALLED and ENABLED outside the throwaway profile, which is why this rule does not yet cite the release gate as its enforcement point

rules.statement: The harness version is pinned exactly in install.sh and install.ps1, and no machine runs an unpinned dsh.
rules.pendingReason: the pins exist in both installers, but no command compares them or refuses an unpinned harness; that check is unbuilt

rules.statement: The deployment's mandatory rules come from $DSH_HOME/AGENTS.md via kit-rules; no repository instruction file reaches the prompt.
A rule is real only where a command fails when it is broken; a rule the kit cannot tie to a failure is reported as an unverified claim.
The kit runs on Linux and Windows; shipped source carries no platform-specific path, separator or binary assumption.
A plugin's tarball is produced by a script, its version is bumped whenever its bytes change, and every module a plugin ships is listed in its package manifest.

A decision enters force only through a human consent recorded against the exact text that was approved; editing an approved record voids the consent, and a record the zone does not authorise is not in force.
The ratification question reaches the human through the harness user-questions channel carrying the record's own text, and no shell command can mint a consent.

An invariant the kit enforces with a command is checked by driving the production modules and requiring the wrong verdict to be refused; no enforcement point rests on a test name or on output a green run prints anyway.

A proposed decision naming a zone satisfies that zone's requiresDecisionRecord and adds no law, so an agent works ahead of a ratification; it never licenses a humanOnly zone and it never licenses work that contradicts a law in force.

Where a ratification question is shown is part of the question: only a grilling session asks it in the Conversation, and every other entry asks for the decision panel, which is a suppression whose absence leaves the harness's own card asking the question rather than leaving it unanswerable.
The ADR panel writes no file and composes no answer: every button it renders sends one of the labels the ratchet itself put in the question, through the one question channel.

verification.purpose: the upgrade and portability gate: throwaway instance, composition, boot and installed-artifact probes
the ratchet's static and dynamic layers, its verdict validation and its gate exit codes
requiresDecisionRecord enforcement: what is refused, what is exempt, and what satisfies the rule

platform assumptions in shipped source; modules missing from a plugin's files list; every packed file matching the source it was packed from, so a stale tarball cannot ship old bytes; and a repack of an existing version carrying a new version, so pnpm cannot serve the old bytes from the lockfile
the ratification seam end to end against a live profile: the question reaches a human channel with the live root agent, answers are derived from labels, and the approval puts the decision into force
the consent surface: no shell mint, no tool argument that accepts an answer, blocked decisions reported with their reason, and retired decisions not queued
instruction routing: the harness workspace-instruction loader is disabled by row id, kit-rules is mounted in its place, it reads only the home rules file, and the installers ship that file

the rules reach an assembled prompt: the shipped kit-rules plugin, applied to the real prompt service, contributes the home AGENTS.md to the rendered prompt, and a second home contributes only its own marker

the ADR panel's browser bundle rendered for real: the shipped client.js is loaded through a stub module loader and driven over the kit's own corpus, asserting the UX contract — three reader-facing sections, states filled and provenance outlined, the awaiting-a-human state in the warn tone, the decided-in chip taking the tone of the record it names, and every toned pill's text resolving through the installed theme to a colour other than its own fill

the gate's own invariants, asserted behaviourally: a law nothing checks is reported, a check that cannot fail is refused, a stream assertion reads each stream as written, a hand-written approval mints nothing, and the code hash moves when the code does
the project-agnostic breaker: break one generic invariant at a time, require the gate to fail, and restore every mutation; writes only inside the declared scopes
the breaker at release-gate scope: break one kit invariant at a time and require the real gate to fail, six cases, each verified to have broken something first
